newsitem.title: USA: US spot MTBE weaker due to volatile NYMEX gasoline.
newsitem.headline: US spot MTBE weaker due to volatile NYMEX gasoline.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices were lower this week amid volatility on NYMEX gasoline futures and continuing high prices for feedstocks, players said on Thursday.
Traders said activity was quiet due to an industry function in New York Harbor and the wide ranges that have been seen in gasoline over the past few days.

NYMEX gasoline was sharply higher on Thursday on rumors of problems at three major Texas refineries, but regulators said they were not yet aware of any problems. Gasoline, however, closed off 0.96 cents, at 68.16 cents a gallon on Wednesday.
"With the Merc jumping up, it's very risky trying to get anything done," said one East Coast broker, adding the market is difficult to gauge.
In the Gulf Coast, spot MTBE was assessed 1.50 cents lower to between 88.00 cents and 88.50 cents a gallon. Deals were traded for 88.00 cents and 88.50 cents earlier in the week.
In New York Harbor, spot MTBE was talked about a half cent lower at 91.00/92.00 in quiet trade. On Thursday Koch Oil sold 35,000 barrels at 91.00 for early November delivery.
Meanwhile, a recent government inventory report on MTBE stocks reported a 10.6 percent fall in inventories to 8.36 million barrels in September.
Traders said the report, which posted draws in the East, West and Gulf Coasts, was very bullish.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
